The nightmare’s dangers reached beyond wounds: souls could be held in candles, and ordinary magic offered no simple way out. That ordeal belonged to the larger mystery around the Guild of Sleep and its stolen Time Stone. The company’s next detour would carry it into its own earlier lives and towards Keraptis’s invitation.

hindsight.title: Crazuk’s candles held more than flame
paragraphs: Humanoids who died in the Nightmare Grotto could have their souls trapped in Crazuk’s candles. Ordinary resurrection could not reach them while they remained confined; destroying the lich and the candles was the way to free them. The domain’s danger extended beyond its walls and exhausting sleep into ownership of the dead.

hindsight.title: The spirit Shrop released was Pengu
paragraphs: The candle Shrop snuffed had confined Pengu. Extinguishing it released the spirit whose influence would drain magic from the world. The failing spells, faltering divine power and waves of anti-magic in Icewind Dale were consequences of that release.

Crazuk’s defeat ended one nightmare, but the released spirit carried another out into the wider world. Pengu’s northern power and the company’s struggle to overcome it began with that candle in the grotto.

scenes.title: The Sleeper and the stolen Time Stone
paragraphs: The Sleeper’s answers tied the dream to Grim’s family. Eudostis Braidedbeard had stolen the Time Stone from the Guild of Sleep in a misguided attempt to free the Sleeper from duty. Removing it had also taken away the lock upon Crimson Crazuk. The attempt to help had forced the Sleeper deeper into the Dream to contain the danger.

Eudostis had carried the Stone away and abandoned adventuring. Much later, Lydzin discovered it, lured him to Rigus, and wished him into the body of a parrot. Years of captivity in a bird’s body had damaged his mind and memory. The Sleeper could repair only part of that harm and urged that he be allowed to rest at home.

Bastion’s investigation had become a story of dreams, stolen time, and an ancestor whose choices still shaped the road. The return to earlier Brindinford made that disturbance personal for all four companions: the company was living through a former part of its own history.

scenes.title: The name on the invitation
paragraphs: The message carried the name Keraptis, an old wizard whose reputation made the challenge more than an ordinary ransom demand. His directions led beneath the feathered plume of the mountain and divided the hunt between three different dangers.

There was a threat beneath the invitation as well. Reaching the weapons was only part of his design; leaving was supposed to be another matter. Keraptis wanted adventurers to enter confident in their own cleverness and discover, too late, whose game they had agreed to play.

image.alt: Black-and-white eight-armed emblem associated with Keraptis
image.caption: Keraptis’s mark, and an invitation with teeth.

scenes.title: Three weapons, three directions
paragraphs: Wave, Whelm, and Blackrazor stood at the heart of the challenge. Keraptis’s clues placed Wave beyond a beast and a boiling bubble; Whelm along a route of chains, double water-spouts, and a cavern; Blackrazor within an inverted ziggurat.

The promise was irresistible, but the weapons had identities of their own. These were legendary, sentient arms, capable of bringing their own wills into the hands that carried them. Even the reward could become another relationship to negotiate.

image.alt: Wave, a luminous blue and silver trident
image.caption: Wave, one of the three legendary weapons named in Keraptis’s challenge.

hindsight.title: A fourth name in the scheme
paragraphs: The names Wave, Whelm and Blackrazor would be joined by a fourth weapon, Frostrazor, in the northern working of the Candle of the Dark One. Bringing all four together required an attunement Keraptis could not achieve himself. Terry’s boon supplied that missing capacity. At the culmination of the Pengu ordeal, Blackrazor—the soul-eating blade—was sacrificed in the ritual.

scenes.title: The mountain failed to keep them
paragraphs: Team Biscuit made it out from beneath White Plume Mountain with loot and magic items. Keraptis’s dungeon had not kept the company, and the return to Brindinford gave them a welcome chance to stop moving and consider what came next.

For a company accustomed to another locked door, another hostile chamber, and another fight beyond the last one, that return mattered. They had survived the mountain and brought its rewards home. The next difficulty waited in a place they already knew.

scenes.title: Brindinford, in simpler times
paragraphs: They were home, in a Brindinford from their own past. The company’s eighth-level selves could walk familiar streets and deal with people whose lives had not yet reached the point the returning adventurers remembered. The question was how to get back to the time they had left.

Their dealings included investments with Shoomma’s smithy and the Bank of Frobozz. Money and equipment were entrusted to the smithy, and a separate pool of silver, electrum, and platinum was set aside for investment with its dwarves. Brindinford was a place to make arrangements as well as a place to seek a way out.

The possibility of staying was part of the temptation. Here were simpler times and a familiar city. Yet the company had unfinished business beyond this borrowed chapter of its life: the Sleeper, the missing souls, and Ashardalon’s hunger had not ceased to matter.

scenes.title: Back—but twenty years beyond their own time
paragraphs: The company eventually made its way back from the flashback, but the return carried it twenty years beyond the original time it had left. Regaining the way forward had not restored the lost present. Two decades now stood between the adventurers and the world they had expected to find.

Brindinford had not survived that absence. A great volcanic cataclysm had collapsed the city, leaving the familiar streets in ruins. The town they had walked as their eighth-level selves—and where they had entrusted investments to Shoomma and the Bank of Frobozz—belonged to a world the catastrophe had broken.

Their business with Shoomma and the Bank of Frobozz belonged to that time-displaced journey. The promises, property, and money left in Brindinford were now part of a much longer absence. The company had returned from an adventure through its own past into a future it had not lived.
Bastion remained unfinished. The detour had changed when the company stood in the world, while the older questions about Ashardalon and the cycle of souls followed it into the years ahead.

hindsight.title: What happened while they were gone
paragraphs: The catastrophe was a delayed consequence of Deep Horizon. The Brotherhood’s rerouting of the lava to save the desmodu village set in motion the disaster that destroyed Brindinford. Across the twenty years the company missed, that same chain of consequences wiped out the entire desmodu race.

The company returned to the aftermath, without having lived through the years between rescue and ruin. A village saved, a city buried, and a people lost: the missing decades had joined what once seemed separate parts of the road.

hindsight.title: Twenty years without new souls
paragraphs: The company’s return carried it twenty years beyond its original present. In the later vision on the ice, the gods named the loss that had marked the world: twenty years without new souls being born. Ashardalon was feeding upon those unborn lives within the Bastion.

The years missing from the company’s journey belonged to a world deprived of its future. Brindinford’s ruin, the loss of the desmodu and the empty cradles were consequences the adventurers returned to face. The cause of the soul famine lay beyond those ruined streets, with the dragon they had yet to reach.

closing.title: The road north from a stolen present
paragraphs: White Plume ended with the company outside the mountain and carrying its rewards. The larger Sleeper detour took it through earlier Brindinford and finally into a world twenty years beyond its original time. The investments, the familiar streets, and the question of getting home belonged to that broken course through history. Brindinford’s volcanic destruction made the missing years a loss of place as well as time.

A warning accused the company of breaking a seal and releasing a primordial menace, then directed it north to repair what had been disturbed. Shrop’s extinguished candle had opened a danger whose consequences would follow them into Icewind Dale. The renewed pursuit of Keraptis and the weapons now ran alongside the need to confront the spirit that had escaped.

The next great journey led into Icewind Dale, where winter held the towns and magic itself was failing. The northern struggle would bring the company against Pengu, the spirit released in the Nightmare Grotto, while Bastion’s unfinished mystery still waited beyond it.

white-plume.eyebrow: The dream, the mountain, and twenty missing years

frostmaiden.title: Beyond the winter, a world at war
opening: The journey into Icewind Dale followed the Sleeper’s time-displaced detour. Team Biscuit now stood twenty years beyond the original time it had left, with Bastion’s mystery still unfinished. In the Dale, winter would not release its hold. Food, shelter, a passable road, and a mine that could work again gave the company immediate work among the people of Ten-Towns.

The road north carried the consequences of a candle snuffed in the Nightmare Grotto. Pengu was free, and magic was failing. Its corruption, the return of Keraptis’s influence and the ruin of Frostblight would carry the company towards a changed world. On the journey home, there would be a besieged keep, an army of demons, and another return to Brindinford.

scenes.title: Ryu, the river, and Terry’s changed voice
paragraphs: The northern road included a confrontation with Grandmaster Ryu Hayabusa. Shrop questioned him in the arctic wasteland, while Thunder watched something unsettling happen to Terry. His companion’s expression had grown vacant; his movements and responses were becoming unnaturally precise.

Terry kept muttering fragments of a numerical riddle. The familiar independence and sarcasm were giving way to a passive, mechanical obedience. The danger was no longer only the enemy before them: something was reaching into the mind of a man the others depended upon.

After Ryu’s last stand, the company travelled for four days in the Brotherhood’s longboats towards Lac Dinneshere and Easthaven. Shrop’s well-chosen tent gave them shelter, but a blizzard on the lake brought remorhaz into the struggle. Ice, weather, and Terry’s continuing change all accompanied the approach to the towns.

scenes.title: Food, ghosts, and the people of the Dale
paragraphs: In Easthaven, the company recovered a cauldron that could help feed the town and returned it to the people. The White Lady’s haunting was laid to rest. Their investigation also exposed duergar activity and the danger surrounding chardalyn, a material whose influence reached well beyond an ordinary mine or hidden cache.

The work carried them through other communities. Near Lonelywood, Thunder tracked the bandit Vorn. In Termalaine, the mine was restored to use. These were victories measured in meals, livelihoods, and the chance to survive another stretch of winter.

They also began gathering the ingredients for the Candle of the Dark One. The search would tie together groves, shrines, dangerous magic, and the growing threat in the far north. The company was already following more than one thread beneath the snow.

image.alt: Snow-covered Easthaven buildings beside the frozen water, their windows glowing in the darkness
image.caption: Easthaven, where a little food and warmth could mean another day.

scenes.title: When the prayers grew faint
paragraphs: North of the Spine of the World, the company’s familiar strengths became less dependable. Magic weakened. Grim’s more powerful spells became almost impossible to call upon; Terry’s connection with Pelor faltered. Arcane learning and divine devotion alike met a world in which the power they needed was ebbing away.

At the Northlook, guidance came through Olaf. Pelor’s message pointed Terry towards the danger gathering in the north. Pengu, linked to the enormous Emperor Penguin statue, was feeding upon Auril’s power and sending waves of anti-magic across the land.

The loss changed more than the force of a spell. A difficult journey, a dangerous wound or a battle beyond the next ridge could no longer be approached with the same confidence in magical aid. The company had to adapt its surviving power to the cold and the creatures ahead. The weakening magic was part of the northern ordeal wherever they went.

The wilderness supplied dangers of its own. The company faced remorhaz, frost giants, and the servants of Auril. Fighting through the cold was hard enough; doing so while spells and divine aid faltered changed the terms of every journey.

hindsight.title: One candle, a world losing its magic
paragraphs: Pengu’s release began when Shrop extinguished the candle in the Nightmare Grotto. In the north, the freed spirit fed upon Auril’s power and sent anti-magic waves across the land. What the company faced in the Dale was the growing consequence of that earlier act.

The cold and the loss of magic reinforced one another. Ten-Towns struggled to survive while the company’s own spells and divine aid faltered. Confronting Pengu meant answering the danger released on the dream-bound road as well as overcoming the enemy waiting at Frostblight.

scenes.title: Wax, wick, and three chances
paragraphs: The Candle of the Dark One required materials with names as melancholy as the Dale itself: Moonlit Sorrow Vine, Ethereal Whispers Blossom, Melancholic Moonstone, Shadowkissed Silk, Whispering Willow Wood, and Mourning Mist Essence. This was a new working sought against Pengu, distinct from the candle Shrop had extinguished in the Nightmare Grotto.

The search took the company among haunted places, the Frostmaiden’s followers, arcane wards, and a mountain shrine. Once the ingredients were gathered, Grim prepared three portions of wax and three wicks. They had the components for three attempts at the candle; the final working still lay ahead.

Meanwhile, Eldath’s guidance drew Shrop towards the Cave of the Berserkers. Frostrazor was there, in the hands of the frost giant Grek. Another trail of legendary weapons was taking shape, and the name Keraptis waited at its centre.

hindsight.title: Terry was the missing key
paragraphs: The hidden key to lighting the candle was Terry’s boon. The working required him to attune to all four weapons of power; Keraptis could manage only three. Possessing the weapons was therefore insufficient for the wizard. Terry himself supplied the possibility his enemy lacked, making the adventurer a potential target for abduction. Gathering the ingredients was one part of the problem; bringing the weapons and the right bearer together was another.

scenes.title: Frostrazor and the false Keraptis
paragraphs: The cave began with a narrow, icy approach and a trap that nearly sent Terry into the ravine. Within waited dragons and berserkers, then Grek with Frostrazor and a cold-burning brazier whose influence had to be broken.

The company divided its effort. Shrop confronted Grek, Terry and Thunder worked to extinguish the brazier, and Grim opposed Keraptis. When the cold flame went out and Grek fell, Frostrazor was recovered. Keraptis’s collapsing body revealed the deception: they had fought a clone.

Before that false body failed, the remaining weapons were linked to the Lost Spire of Netheril. White Plume’s old name had followed the company north, but this encounter had not put an end to the wizard behind it. The victory gave them a weapon and another destination.

scenes.title: The raid on Easthaven
paragraphs: Pengu’s army brought the northern threat into the town. Mutated emperor penguins struck Easthaven while a blizzard delayed the company’s response. Much of the southern town was left in ruins, and people who had survived the long winter were killed in the raid.

The storm made the distance cruel. Knowing where help was needed did not mean the company could reach it in time. The place whose food supply they had helped secure had become the scene of a different disaster.

Olaf supplied a map to the Lost Spire of Netheril, giving the company a lead when the way forward had grown uncertain. The hunt for the weapons and the struggle against the northern corruption continued towards the ruins and Frostblight.

image.alt: A horde of penguin creatures near a devastated northern settlement
image.caption: The penguin army turned an absurd shape into a very real terror.

scenes.title: The Lost Spire and Dannika’s Darlings
paragraphs: The Lost Spire of Netheril held more than the trail of the weapons. In its depths, Vellynne Harpell stood with Dannika’s Darlings remade as undead servants: Dannika, Filverel, Dodo, and Uldruc. Their familiar names now belonged to another necromancer’s force.

The company fought Vellynne and her corrupted champions. The chamber’s golden disk and ancient workings offered mysteries of their own, but first there were enemies to survive. Even a promising book could be bait: a freshly labelled volume of Secrets of the Arcane Brotherhood concealed blank pages and Vellynne’s name.

The pursuit of Keraptis had drawn them towards the spire; the confrontation there put necromancy and the fate of another adventuring company in their path. The later vision on the ice would invoke the legendary weapons again, drawing the northern journey back towards the challenge beneath White Plume Mountain.

scenes.title: Gnometti’s kitchen in the ice
paragraphs: Frostblight had a host as well as a tyrant. Gnometti, its little gnome chef, wore an immaculate uniform in a kitchen where the cold had settled into the cook himself. A bluish pallor lay beneath his skin, frost gathered at his cuffs, and his cheerful manner had the polish of a welcome repeated for far too many winters.

His business was food, recipes and the troublesome appetites of the creatures outside. Ice Seal Meals could pacify the territorial seals guarding the caves; preserved fish, saltwater and dried seaweed were the practical ingredients behind that small advantage. Among monstrous rulers and failing spells, the gnome offered the thoroughly domestic possibility that a dangerous passage might be negotiated with supper.

The warmth belonged to his hospitality rather than his hands. Gnometti’s brittle, frost-preserved appearance made his little kitchen another unsettling part of Pengu’s realm: something familiar continuing far beyond the life it ought to have had. Beyond the recipes and the cooking pot waited the power that had made this place a prison.

image.alt: Gnometti, the white-bearded ice gnome chef, in his original Roll20 portrait token
image.caption: Gnometti: chef, keeper of recipes, and a remarkably cheerful presence in Frostblight’s frozen dark.

scenes.title: Terry, four weapons, and Blackrazor’s sacrifice
paragraphs: The northern quest had gathered its answer one piece at a time. Moonlit Sorrow Vine, Ethereal Whispers Blossom, Melancholic Moonstone, Shadowkissed Silk, Whispering Willow Wood and Mourning Mist Essence had become the materials for the Wax and Wick of the Dark One. Grim had prepared three portions of wax and three wicks. The search through the Dale now reached the working those preparations had been meant to make possible.

The four epic weapons were brought together: Wave, Whelm, Frostrazor and Blackrazor. Their trail had begun beneath White Plume Mountain and continued through Keraptis’s schemes into the frozen north. Treasure that had once promised power to its bearers had become part of an answer to Pengu.

Terry supplied what Keraptis could not. Pelor’s Boon of Attunement allowed him to bind himself to all four weapons at once, beyond the three the wizard could manage. The boon became the key to the candle working. The company’s hope rested upon the dwarf whose faith had endured the very loss of magic they had come to end.

The ritual demanded a sacrifice. Blackrazor, the blade that fed upon souls, was given up. Its hunger had made it a terrible prize; now the company surrendered it as the cost of the rite. Wave, Whelm and Frostrazor remained to continue along their road. Blackrazor did not.

The working was completed. The ingredients, the hunt for the weapons and Terry’s extraordinary attunement had reached their purpose. A candle snuffed in the Nightmare Grotto had released Pengu; the company had now answered that catastrophe with a ritual of its own, and with a sacrifice it could not simply put back in a scabbard.

scenes.title: Pengu’s last shape
paragraphs: Frostblight’s final struggle brought the company against the creatures Pengu had remade. Corrupted emperors, Panguini and Dreamkeepers stood along the way. Mad Kaelith fell during the fighting. At the heart of the stronghold waited Pengu, bound upon a throne of jagged ice, black runed chains stretching from her body into the frozen walls.

The spirit Shrop had released from the grotto’s candle was now before them. Its influence had weakened the world’s magic, twisted the northern creatures and turned Auril’s power against the land. Terry’s fourfold attunement and the sacrifice of Blackrazor belonged to the company’s answer; the battle brought that long pursuit to its final, immediate danger.

When the final blow landed, Pengu’s great form convulsed and folded inward. Her body compressed until the enormous presence upon the battlefield had become a black egg ten feet tall, gleaming like liquid obsidian. The chamber fell silent around a slow, deliberate heartbeat.

Each pulse drew warmth from the air. Frost crept across the floor, and the egg’s reflective surface returned distorted glimpses of the companions. Pengu’s fighting form had fallen. What remained was a vessel still alive with the power that had filled the stronghold.

Then Frostblight came apart. The monumental penguin statue cracked and shattered; stone and ice fell through the ruin of the frozen citadel. The company’s victory became an escape as the ice shelf broke beneath the way out. They plunged into the arctic sea and survived upon an isolated iceberg, with sheer ice above the water and no land in sight.

The northern ordeal had reached its reckoning: the ritual completed, Blackrazor sacrificed, Pengu defeated and Frostblight broken. The company had survived the end of the enemy’s frozen dominion. Around its little refuge lay the sea; beyond it waited the first promise that the world’s magic could begin to heal.

image.alt: A huge penguin monument beneath the aurora, surrounded by an army in the snow
image.caption: Frostblight’s monument, before the ice and stone gave way.

hindsight.title: Mad Kaelith had once been a queen
paragraphs: Kaelith had once been Aeloria Frostsong, the compassionate queen who led the Panguini against Pengu. The invasion broke her resistance and her mind, turning her into the enforcer of the power she had tried to stop. The enemy the company faced carried the ruined history of an earlier defender of this realm.

hindsight.title: What the egg still held
paragraphs: The obsidian egg retained a heartbeat and an unnatural hunger for warmth. Pengu’s defeat and the destruction of Frostblight ended this northern reign, but the surviving vessel carried a possibility beyond that victory. Within it, something still waited. Its later fate was another thread left beyond the company’s escape.

scenes.title: A vision on the ice
paragraphs: On the ice, the company’s dream brought Pelor, Eldath, and Auril together. Eldath spoke of magic healing gradually after its long suppression. Pengu’s defeat had allowed the flow to begin returning, but the world would need time to regain its strength. Auril acknowledged how Pengu had made a prison of her domain. From the grotto’s extinguished candle to the breaking of Frostblight, the company had followed a calamity it had helped set loose and fought to overcome.

Recovery did not end every crisis. The vision returned the company to Ashardalon’s hunger for souls. The gods spoke of twenty years in which no new souls had been born into the world. Magic could begin to flow again while the dragon continued consuming unborn lives; the road back to Bastion remained urgent.

The gods’ message called them back towards Rigus. The crisis of births without souls had continued while they struggled in the north. The Bastion mystery they had begun before that journey was still waiting, and the world could not afford for it to remain unanswered.

For Thunder, the dream also held the Deliverance and Captain Timothy Pepper. The Pendant of the Ethereal Anchor bound Thunder’s soul to the ghostly ship. Pepper had warned him of its price: dying while wearing it would make Thunder the ship’s captive captain in Pepper’s place. In the vision, the ship endured and searched for him; that reassurance did not remove the bargain.

Another guide appeared beneath the ice: Angajuk, the great whale, offering passage onward. Deliverance and whale would carry different parts of the company’s story. The promise of a way forward led from the frozen sea towards the planes.

scenes.title: Through the Maw, into Acheron
paragraphs: The way out of the northern waters led towards a strange gateway beneath a sea that had fallen unnaturally still. Ancient runes marked the chasm called the Silent Maw. Beyond the ordeal of the Hungry Maw, the company’s next awakening was aboard a vessel resting on Angajuk’s back, with silver mist surrounding them where the sea should have been.

Angajuk was adrift in the Astral Sea until a distant rhythm gave direction: the sound of forgework reaching through the void. The passage carried them past broken cities, shattered titans, and relics of old wars. Ahead lay a vast iron cube scarred by trenches, with a fortress of red stone at its centre.

The whale would go no farther. Angajuk opened a rift, and the company passed through into gravity, heat, smoke, and iron. They had reached Acheron again. The Red Keep waited below, holding a history of the company’s absence that none of the northern victories had prepared them to meet.

scenes.title: What had happened to Rigus
paragraphs: Beyond the northern ordeal waited news of a world that had not stood still. Father Cuthbert’s Chronicle of the Reclamation told of Rigus after the company’s departure: magic had failed, the wards had collapsed, and demons had poured through the broken Lion’s Gate. The city fell in less than a week.

Cuthbert also recorded a quieter catastrophe: infants born without souls and resurrection magic faltering. The company had heard of the failing cycle of life before leaving Rigus. The chronicle showed that the danger had endured through the city’s fall and the refugees’ flight. Defeating an army could not, by itself, restore those missing lives.

Cuthbert led survivors towards the Red Keep. There, a relic touched by Pelor’s fire became the heart of the Cold Forge. Those who died defending the Keep could rise again within it. Refugees, warriors, and Formacid allies gathered around that miracle, and the Church of the Reclamation took shape.

The company they remembered had become the Blessed Company. Shrines had been raised to them; Terry’s armour had been found waiting. While the adventurers fought through the north, other people had built a faith around their absence. Coming back meant meeting the weight of what they had become to those who survived.

hindsight.title: The hunger behind the silent cradles
paragraphs: Pengu’s suppression of magic reached beyond Icewind Dale. When Rigus’s arcane and divine wards failed, the Lion’s Gate broke and the demons entered. The disaster Shrop’s candle had released helped strip the city of its defenses. The returning company met survivors whose war had begun in that magical collapse.

Ashardalon was consuming souls before they could be born, feeding his failing demonic heart at the Bastion of Unborn Souls. The absent spark in the infants was the consequence of that predation reaching across the worlds. Cuthbert’s chronicle records the suffering among the living; the dragon’s feast explains what had been taken before those lives could begin. The northern vision named twenty years without new souls. The company’s return to Rigus brought that warning among survivors whose own losses had become a chronicle.

These dangers had different sources. Pengu’s release brought the loss of magic; Ashardalon’s feeding stole unborn souls. Breaking Pengu’s hold allowed magic to recover, but the dragon’s predation continued. The victory in the north could open the road back to Bastion without finishing the work waiting there.

scenes.title: The Red Keep and the general’s cell
paragraphs: By the time of the return, the Red Keep had endured a prolonged demonic siege. Its defenders held because the walls, the Formacid tunnels, and the Cold Forge gave them a way to resist losses that should have broken them. Father Cuthbert kept the rite alive by faith and memory.

General Nagaro’s arrival brought another wound from Rigus. The former commander came to the Keep injured, under suspicion of having fled before the city’s fall. Placed in protective custody, she was found dead by morning. Her death left an accusation without a settled answer.

On the fifteenth of Marpenoth, 1406, Cuthbert recorded the Blessed Company’s return in the flesh. For the people who had made shrines to them, this was the return of living saints. For Team Biscuit, it meant stepping into a war, a church, and a mystery already waiting behind the walls.

scenes.title: The demon army
paragraphs: The enemy beyond the Keep was an army. Vrocks, hezrous, glabrezus, chasmes, and nalfeshnees formed part of the fighting, while greater horrors included goristros, mariliths, and balors. The company had reached a battlefield crowded with powers that could each have filled a nightmare on their own.

Alongside them fought Iron Fang veterans, Crimson Scorcher veterans, Spirewatch archers, and Blightspike skirmishers. Beast-handlers brought their own menagerie into the struggle: giant scorpions, a bulette, a shambling mound, and a hydra. This force combined disciplined fighters, monsters, and the strength of the Abyss.

Team Biscuit fought through that army. The struggle extended beyond a single clash or a single great demon; its later fighting reached an Ultroloth Ascendant, who fell before the company. The road from the Dale had carried them into a war for the survivors of Rigus, and the company had met its armies in person.
Brindinford was still ahead. Before they could call the journey home complete, the company would find another familiar place transformed—and another company already caught in its troubles.

closing.title: Home, beneath the streets
paragraphs: The northern expedition had begun with hungry towns, haunted waters and a winter that would not end. Beneath those troubles ran the consequence of Shrop’s candle in the Nightmare Grotto. The answer demanded rare ingredients, four epic weapons, Terry’s boon and the sacrifice of Blackrazor. Pengu’s defeat and the breaking of Frostblight brought that struggle to its climax; the gods’ vision promised magic’s gradual return. The pulsing egg remained beyond the victory, and the Red Keep’s survivors still faced the demon army that had followed Rigus’s fall.

At the end of the Icewind Dale journey, the way home led into Fungus Grotto and sunken Brindinford. There, Shrop, Grim, Terry, and Thunder would fight alongside Team Gravy—Brunn, Rook, Nox, and Elira—against giant ants among the buried remnants of a city they knew. The next passage belongs to both companies.

bastion.title: The road returns to the dragon
opening: Ashardalon had been part of this story long before the company could reach him. His name lay beneath the Citadel, above the dead of Nightfang Spire, and behind a sickness that left newborn children without souls. The Cathezar’s pursuit had made the danger personal. The Church of the Elements, the First Tree, and the Guild of Sleep had begun to give it a shape.

Then the road had wandered through dreams, earlier lives, and a return twenty years beyond the time they had left. There had been investments laid against an uncertain future, the northern winter, the Red Keep, the demon army, and the buried streets of Brindinford. The company had carried its unfinished business through all of it.

On the ice, the gods had spoken of twenty years without new souls being born into the world. Pengu’s defeat had allowed magic to begin healing, but Ashardalon was still feeding. The company returned to a world whose stolen future waited beyond the dragon’s refuge.
Now Shrop, Grim, Terry, and Thunder returned to the question waiting beneath those adventures: how could four mortals reach a dragon feeding upon lives that had not yet begun?

scenes.title: An old shop, a new world
paragraphs: The Reality Wrinkle had survived where much of Brindinford had fallen. Team Biscuit and Team Gravy had fought through the giant ants of the Sunken City to reach the old Magical District. There, a portal trap intended for Team Biscuit caught Brunn, Rook, Nox and Elira instead. Team Gravy were sent to Hell and remain lost there; Team Biscuit’s onward road led to Windglum.

The crossing delivered Team Biscuit into a cramped storeroom. Brindinford crates, ash-marked trunks, cracked scroll tubes, and old papers crowded the shelves. Much of what the Wrinkle’s mages had once brought here was gone. Outside, the wind screamed through Pandemonium.

The party had reached Windglum. Its next shelter was the room beyond the great mirror at the back of the Wrinkle, a hidden corner in a city far from the world it remembered. The ants and the ruined streets were behind them; the road to the Bastion had opened again.

scenes.title: Findula finds the way
paragraphs: Findula was waiting among the travel chests, a small harp across her lap. The lillend was an old ally whose freedom had cost the company effort and danger. She had a debt to repay, and the means of repayment would lead them towards Eco, the guardian of a much older prison.

Windglum offered a pause. Equipment could be replaced, wounds could close, and the crooked stalls could occupy adventurers who had spent too long away from a market. At night, the company returned through the mirror to bedrolls among the crates. Findula came and went, following traces and studying the difficult roads between worlds.

At last she summoned them to the backroom. A cleared table held a map, candles, and a strange compass with trembling crystal points. Her search had found Eco. The path would not remain fixed: the guardian’s location changed every day, and Findula could offer a way through only while the trace held. Preparations in Windglum suddenly had a deadline.

scenes.title: The guardian who was the door
paragraphs: Eco stood between the company and Desayeus, the God Who Was Banned. A solar accompanied by the planetar Bramam, she had guarded the prison for centuries. No hidden tunnel or convenient spell could replace her. Her own body could become the gateway.

The company sought permission. Shrop pressed the question of whether Eco could open the way under divine command; Pelor’s answer granted passage to speak with the prisoner, while expressly forbidding his release. They were to enter carefully and leave his chains alone.

Grim carried that distinction into the audience. The company came seeking counsel and aid against Ashardalon. It did not announce itself as Desayeus’s liberator. For a moment, a problem older than kingdoms had been approached with the surprisingly delicate instrument of a properly worded request.

hindsight.title: A life bound into the lock
paragraphs: Eco’s guardianship carried a terrible provision: her death would open the passage for three days. She was both a person and the prison’s only living entrance. That made violence a possible way through, but it never made her an ordinary obstacle. Nor would an open doorway free Desayeus or the Faithful; the prison’s binding still held them.

scenes.title: The god who remembered his name
paragraphs: Desayeus waited in a prison worn down by centuries. Broken instruments, ruined art, and the devotion of his remaining Faithful surrounded a being who had once been worshipped. His immense body still carried the bearing of a god. The fractured pendant at his chest carried what remained of his claim.

Grim and Thunder questioned him about the Bastion, the dragon, and the Soul Totem. Desayeus had been divine before he claimed dominion over the unborn. The other gods had stripped him of that divinity and broken the Totem. One fragment remained with him; another had provided Ashardalon with a way into the Bastion.

The company needed the piece he still wore. Its request touched the last remnant of an office he had lost, and the last possession he could hold against his judges. Grim asked to borrow it. Thunder brought the danger back to his own blood, hunted because of Dydd and seeking a way to end the fate that pursued him.

hindsight.title: Why the gods left mortals at the threshold
paragraphs: The Ban of the Unborn forbade divine interference with souls before incarnation. Desayeus’s attempt to claim them had brought the other gods down upon him. Their fear of that same prohibition helped leave the Bastion beyond the aid mortals might expect from prayer. Pelor’s permission concerned Eco’s doorway; it was no promise that a god would enter the Bastion and finish the company’s work.

scenes.title: The price of the fragment
paragraphs: The passage through the prison did not end as a simple exchange of questions and answers. By the time the company prepared to leave, Eco was defeated and gone. Desayeus had yielded his fragment of the Soul Totem. Thunder carried the small, heavy thing upon which the next journey depended.
The fragment was theirs. Desayeus remained behind. Around the company lay the ruined chambers of a prison whose silence now carried another loss.

They still had to return through Pandemonium to the Wrinkle. Beyond that lay the Positive Energy Plane and the Bastion itself. The means of continuing had been won, but the cost followed them out of the prison.

scenes.title: A debt paid in grief
paragraphs: When the company returned to the hidden room, Findula had gone. Her papers, instruments, and personal belongings had disappeared from among the familiar clutter. A folded note waited at the centre of the table.

Eco had been her sister. Findula had neither raised the blade nor opened the door herself, but she accepted that her choices had helped bring about Eco’s death. She believed stopping Ashardalon justified that terrible cost. Belief had not made it bearable, and repayment had not left affection intact.
She considered her debt settled. She did not expect to speak with the company again, and did not wish to. The farewell left Team Biscuit with a path forward and an ally it could no longer count upon.

image.alt: Findula’s handwritten farewell, grieving Eco and declaring her debt to the party paid
image.caption: Findula’s farewell: the cost carried back from the prison. The folded page ends an alliance the company once had good reason to trust.

scenes.title: The man who had survived the explosion
paragraphs: Another familiar face met them with a very different welcome. Brother Ernie had been lost amid the dangerous business of the irionite bomb. The company had believed the explosion had taken him. Now he was here, weathered and battered, surrounded by boxes, trunks, bottles, books, clothing, and much of their recovered property.

These were the possessions Xanthar’s deception had cost them. He had persuaded Team Biscuit to use the portal to the grotto, where they arrived naked and without their equipment. Ernie’s return finally joined that humiliating loss to its unlikely recovery, though it offered no rescue for the friends still lost in Hell.

There were questions about Rigus, Father Cuthbert, the Brotherhood, and the Church of Terry. Grim wanted to know how Ernie had survived and how he had crossed the planes. Ernie greeted them with his old broad smile and applied himself to the explanation with gestures and an interpretive dance of magnificent commitment and uncertain informational value.

Most of the stolen belongings had come back. Three great weapons had not: Whelm, Wave and Frostrazor. Blackrazor had already been sacrificed in the ritual against Pengu; it was no longer a possession for Ernie to recover. Ernie’s apologetic chalk drawing showed a short thief carrying the remaining three away. Grim suspected a connection to his relative, but suspicion could not put the weapons back into their hands.

image.alt: Brother Ernie smiling in an upstairs room crowded with recovered trunks, equipment, and belongings
image.caption: An old friend, an improbable return, and most of the missing luggage. The smile was familiar even after a journey no interpretive dance could adequately explain.

scenes.title: Four rings and a silent farewell
paragraphs: Ernie’s last gift was practical enough to matter beyond the reunion. He gave each member of Team Biscuit a Ring of Positive Energy Protection, a ward for the realm they would have to cross. The journey ahead led into a place where life itself could kill an unprotected traveller.
He presented the rings without a speech. There were embraces, and then a departure through the office door. Warm motes of light gathered around the old friend as he faded from sight.

The disappearance offered no tidy account of what Ernie was or where he was going. It left the company with his gifts, their recovered possessions, and the memory of a man who had returned from an explosion to help them once more.

image.alt: Brother Ernie walking through a doorway as warm golden motes gather around his cloak
image.caption: Ernie’s departure left its own mystery. The company kept his gifts while the meaning of that departure remained its own mystery.

scenes.title: Into too much life
paragraphs: With the Soul Totem fragment, the company could follow the road beyond Windglum. The shard served as the focus for their passage and the guide through the brilliance beyond it. Pandemonium’s screaming winds gave way to the white expanse of the Positive Energy Plane.

Here there was no ordinary ground or sky. A traveller chose a direction to become down, then fell through the light. The same energy that closed wounds pressed more life into a mortal body than it could safely contain. Healing and destruction stood dangerously close together.

The fragment drew them towards a vast crystalline form: the Bastion of Unborn Souls, spread across the radiance like an immense snowflake. Somewhere within its branching halls, souls gathered before their first lives. Somewhere deeper, Ashardalon was feeding.

image.alt: Campaign illustration of an immense branching crystal Bastion in the brilliance of the Positive Energy Plane
image.caption: The Bastion of Unborn Souls, in the campaign’s travel illustration. Within its radiant branches, the company’s oldest unfinished questions waited beside lives not yet begun.

scenes.title: The entrance had teeth
paragraphs: Reaching the Bastion did not mean entering it unopposed. Fiends had gathered at the approach, and an enormous spiderlike retriever guarded the way. The company had come carrying a key; the creatures waiting outside had no intention of making its use easy.

Glabrezu, a hezrou, and a nalfeshnee joined the fighting. The retriever struck with great claws and rays of destructive magic. Grim’s chain lightning leapt among the attackers while the others fought through the space around the guardian.

The struggle carried into the next advance, until the retriever and the fiends barring the entrance were overcome. The Soul Totem fragment gave the company a way through the sealed portal. Behind the threshold waited a fortress whose inhabitants had made the birthplace of souls into contested ground.

scenes.title: Dragonspawn among the crystal trees
paragraphs: Inside, Po, Krushar, and Thalidorus met the intruders. The defenders brought blades, axes, jaws, and fire into the crystal halls. Po issued challenges across the fighting; Krushar’s two heads and paired weapons made a brutal answer to anyone trying to hold the way.

Then Grisly came out of the grove. The half-dragon bear added another furnace of breath and a crushing weight of claws to an encounter already crowded with enemies. The beautiful crystal growth offered cover for something thoroughly capable of tearing an adventurer apart.

The company broke through. Po fell, followed by Grisly, Krushar, and Thalidorus. Their defeat opened the route deeper into the Bastion. The party searched what the fallen had carried, reclaimed useful protections and weapons, and continued towards the thing at the centre of it all.

image.alt: Campaign portrait of the armoured dragonspawn Po
image.caption: Po, one of the defenders within the Bastion.

scenes.title: Predators in the birthplace of souls
paragraphs: Four soulsippers waited along the company’s advance. Their attacks drained life in the very place where life should have been beginning. Team Biscuit destroyed them and pressed onwards, but the grove’s defenders were only the beginning of the resistance within the Bastion.

Farther in, the fighting reached the Cuckoo’s demon guard and Tamion’s ambush. A vrock’s screech cut through the battle. Tamion’s long whip could drag a victim into its grip. The halls demanded another expenditure of magic, endurance, and the company’s stubborn refusal to stop.

Terry was driven down during the later fighting. Around the battered company, the Bastion remained occupied and dangerous. Every chamber won brought them closer to Ashardalon; no chamber won could answer what would happen when they reached him.

scenes.title: The blood the dragon feared
paragraphs: Thunder had carried the answer to one part of the mystery within him. Dydd, the druid who had mortally wounded Ashardalon’s heart, was his ancestor. That bloodline had drawn the Cathezar’s pursuit and made him useful to powers whose interest in the dragon had nothing to do with saving children.

In Desayeus’s prison he had already spoken the challenge: he named Dydd, claimed their shared blood, and called upon the dragon to feel the pain of its heart’s destruction again. The words belonged to a reckoning older than the company, now carried by one of its own.

The lineage did not walk into the Bastion alone. Shrop had fought his way here without sight, Grim had argued with a fallen god, and Terry had carried faith into a conflict where divine permission came with limits. Whatever Dydd’s blood could do, four companions had brought it within reach of Ashardalon.

scenes.title: What beat inside Ashardalon
paragraphs: At the centre of the mystery stood a dragon who had survived his own ruined heart. Across tombs, fortresses, dreams, and planes, the company had followed the consequences of that survival. The stolen future of the unborn had become the means by which Ashardalon prolonged his life.

The Bastion had been a font of souls before the dragon claimed it. His presence had turned its abundance into a famine elsewhere. Every road the company had followed now narrowed towards a creature sustained by the lives the world was waiting to receive.

image.alt: Campaign portrait of Ashardalon, the ancient red dragon
image.caption: Ashardalon: the ancient hunger at the heart of the journey.

hindsight.title: The replacement heart had a name
paragraphs: Ashardalon’s replacement heart was Ammet, Eater of Souls, a demon bound within the dragon. That transplant was failing. Consuming the Bastion’s raw life force sustained Ashardalon and made him dependent upon remaining at its centre. His hoard had become the supply keeping him alive; the lives he consumed were souls that had never reached birth.

The vision after Frostblight had named twenty years without new souls. Pengu’s loss of magic and Ashardalon’s feeding were different calamities: the first could begin to heal while the dragon continued consuming the unborn. Reaching the Bastion meant confronting the hunger that the northern victory had not ended.

hindsight.title: A second predator wanted the prize
paragraphs: Aameul, one of Demogorgon’s two minds, wanted Ammet’s soul strengthened by that stolen life. With it, he hoped to survive the destruction of Hethradiah and exist alone. His agents’ search for Dydd’s descendant was part of that design. A blow against Ashardalon could threaten one monster while serving another, and the demon within the dragon carried a danger of his own.

closing.title: Beyond the last door
paragraphs: The journey had begun with missing adventurers and a ruined fortress beneath Oakhurst. It had brought four companions to a place where the future of countless strangers waited in crystal branches. Ashardalon’s hunger, Dydd’s old wound, and the ambitions of the Abyss had met at the same door.

What becomes of the dragon when his stolen refuge is challenged? What becomes of Ammet when the heart that imprisons him is threatened? And will the souls denied their first breath find their way into the world? Those answers belong to the reckoning at the centre of the Bastion.

Beyond that reckoning lie other unfinished threads: three missing weapons, a silent friend’s departure, Findula’s grief, investments waiting across the years, and the homes to which the company might yet return. There is room for the world to change again—and for Team Biscuit to discover what, after all this, it means to come home.
